correctness.rationale: The joint density of two successful passage durations is uv exp[-(u+d1)x-(v+d2)y]. Changing to completion time produces a sinhc kernel whose argument is (u-v+d1-d2)s/2 and whose prefactor and total exit-rate sum are invariant under swapping investments. Its strictly increasing absolute-argument response proves strict pointwise successful-completion density ordering for all positive times, hence all bounded nonnegative nontrivial rewards, while a strict derivative at parity excludes a balanced optimum when hazards differ. For equal hazards, the success prefactor and classical fixed-rate-sum stochastic order of a two-exponential completion time both favor equal investment for nonincreasing rewards. A uniform differentiated integral expansion proves the second-order short-horizon bias and short-horizon uniqueness; log strict concavity of eventual success and dominated C2 convergence prove the long-horizon maximizer and eventual uniqueness. The delivered checker separately integrates the two-stage density and the exact single-integral formula and tests 1494 sampled cases; numerical checks are not substitutes for the proof.

originality.rationale: On the inspected material, ecological connectivity indicators and stepping-stone models do not solve constrained two-stage competing death versus travel for all time rewards. Existing exponential-convolution stochastic-order results cover a conditional equal-hazard ingredient but not, by themselves, the unconditional opposite-hazard swap inequality with arbitrary rewards and budget-constrained short/long deadline asymptotics. Closest published network allocations instead optimize multi-patch extinction times, stationarity or multi-customer queues. Priority remains provisional pending a broader survey of historical reliability, stochastic-control, and queueing optimization work.
residual_risks: Historical priority is provisional because the search is bounded and many earlier reliability, stochastic-control or applied probability allocation results may not be indexed.
The 2024 three-patch metapopulation hub-effect article was accessible only by abstract; its different reversible dynamics suggest noncoverage but its full text was not inspected.
No independent expert audit or empirical habitat parameter calibration has been performed.

value.rationale: In conservation corridor interventions it matters not only whether links exist but which mortality bottleneck to improve under finite total rate improvement. The theorem establishes a universal, directionally sharp inequality independent of the deadline or time-reward function, complementing habitat connectivity and metapopulation priority literature; its second-order short-time coefficient and closed-form eventual allocation quantify the investment-bias scale. This is a substantive structural result in a natural two-bottleneck passage model, not a mere numerical gain, table entry or arbitrary parameter slice. Applicability is limited by independent memoryless clocks and rate-sum costs.
